QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_35

question.text: How do dividends affect equity futures pricing versus other asset class futures?

answer.text: Expected dividends reduce equity futures prices below what cost-of-carry alone would predict; currency futures use interest rate differentials (no dividends); commodity futures use finance/storage costs less convenience yield where relevant (no dividends)
Dividends affect all derivative markets equally
Dividends have no impact on any futures pricing

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity futures: F = S(1 + r - q)^T discretely, or F = S x e^((r - q) x T) continuously, where q is the dividend yield — higher dividends mean a lower futures price relative to spot. Currency futures: F = S x e^((r - rf) x T) (or the equivalent interest-rate-differential discrete form). Commodity futures incorporate finance and storage costs less convenience yield where relevant. The Trap: Dividends reduce equity futures because carrying the stock earns them, lowering net carry; this dividend adjustment is unique to equity futures and does not apply to currency or interest-rate futures. Note: Commodity carry is not storage-only — for many commodities the pricing model includes finance and storage costs minus a convenience yield where applicable.
